summary: Registers image/t38 as a MIME media type for real-time fax. The encoding itself is defined by ITU-T T.38 and is intended for use as an SDP media descriptor.

plainLanguage.summary: Faxes can now be sent over internet calls. This document registers the official label for that kind of fax data so programs know what it is.

how is t38 fax described in sdp
what is real-time facsimile over ip

subtitle: Official MIME type for real-time faxing over the internet.

tldr.problem: Real-time faxing over IP needed a standard way to identify fax data streams in internet call protocols, but there was no official MIME type for this.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3362 registers the image/t38 MIME media type for T.38 real-time facsimile communication, intended for use in SDP (Session Description Protocol) media descriptors within SIP call setup.
tldr.outcome: The image/t38 MIME type is now standard for describing T.38 fax streams in VoIP protocols, enabling fax transmission over IP networks.

today: RFC 3362 is a Proposed Standard that defines the image/t38 MIME type used in VoIP systems for T.38 real-time faxing. The MIME type remains in use in IP-based telephony systems that support fax transmission.

sections.title: T.38 Real-Time Faxing
sections.content:
ITU-T Recommendation T.38 defines how to send faxes in real-time between standard Group 3 facsimile terminals over the internet using IP protocols. It allows the use of either TCP or UDP depending on the service environment. RFC 3362 registers the image/t38 MIME media type for T.38 facsimile data.

The encoding itself is defined by the T.38 standard. The MIME type registration is intended for use as a Session Description Protocol (SDP) media descriptor in SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) call setup for internet-based faxing.
sections.plainLanguage: The internet can now handle faxes in real-time, and this document gives that fax data an official name that programs understand.

sections.title: MIME Type Registration
sections.content:
The image/t38 MIME type is registered with the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). The media type is named image with a subtype of t38. The media type has no required or optional parameters and uses binary encoding.

The T.38 specification defines the actual encoding and procedures for real-time facsimile communication. The MIME type is not intended for email usage; it is specifically designed for use in SIP-based voice call protocols to establish and describe fax sessions.
sections.plainLanguage: The official name is image/t38. It's for real-time faxing in phone calls, not for email attachments.

sections.title: Security and Interoperability
sections.content:
A T.38 facsimile bit stream may or may not be encrypted, depending on the implementation and deployment. The image/t38 media type itself does not enforce encryption, though T.38 implementations may support it.

The MIME type is specifically intended for use in SDP media descriptors in SIP call setup as described in ITU-T T.38 Annex D. Using this media type in email applications or other contexts is not defined and is not guaranteed to interoperate with actual T.38 streams.
sections.plainLanguage: Fax data can be encrypted if needed, but that's up to the system using it. This media type is only for phone calls, not other uses.
